_comment: BoGo disable ledger. run-bogo.sh runs the whole suite; every test must PASS or match
a glob here. Each reason starts with its bucket, which the runner classifies:
[out-of-scope] skipped; [policy-difference] force-run and asserted to still differ (a
now-passing one is a stale disable); [deferred] skipped. Keys are glob patterns (*)
over the test name; the peer is pinned by BOGO_REF.
REVIEW RULE: any NEW or broadened [out-of-scope]/[deferred] glob must be reviewed to
confirm it cannot match an in-scope (modern-TLS) test. The per-push over_match check
catches a glob that shadows a still-PASSING test, but a glob shadowing a would-FAIL
test is invisible to the gate (a disabled test never runs) - it is caught only here, at
review. Prefer version-anchored patterns (e.g. *-TLS12) over version-agnostic prefixes.
_comment_halfrtt: This shim issues its NewSessionTickets at 1-RTT (after the client Finished), not at
half-RTT like BoringSSL, so on a 0-RTT accept the runner must expect zero half-RTT
tickets before the half-RTT data. The 0.5-RTT early-data echo still rides out normally.

DisabledTests.*EarlyData-UnfinishedWrite-Client-*: [out-of-scope] BoringSSL async partial-write API: SSL_write returns WANT_WRITE mid-early-data-write and the shim reads/responds before completing it (-read-with-unfinished-write). A synchronous sans-IO engine buffers whole writes, so an 'unfinished write' has no analog; the 0-RTT wire behavior is covered by the non-async EarlyData tests
DisabledTests.*EarlyData-RejectUnfinishedWrite-Client-: [out-of-scope] BoringSSL async partial-write API (-read-with-unfinished-write) on a 0-RTT reject: the rejected unfinished write is discarded by the calling app. No analog for a synchronous sans-IO engine; the reject/replay-discard wire behavior is covered by the non-async EarlyData-Reject tests
DisabledTests.EarlyData-WriteAfterServerHello: [out-of-scope] BoringSSL async mid-handshake write timing (-async -on-resume-early-write-after-message ServerHello): the app writes early data only after a specific server message arrives, so it lands as 1-RTT. The synchronous shim writes before driving the handshake; the late-write-as-1-RTT wire behavior is covered by the TooMuchData over-budget overflow tests
DisabledTests.EarlyData-WriteAfterEncryptedExtensions: [out-of-scope] BoringSSL async mid-handshake write timing (-async -on-resume-early-write-after-message EncryptedExtensions); as EarlyData-WriteAfterServerHello, no analog for a synchronous sans-IO shim

The -0/-6/-9 cases our default order already satisfies

DisabledTests.MaxCBCPadding: [policy-difference] AEAD-only posture: the CBC suite (ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA) this exercises is not offered; rustls is likewise AEAD-only
DisabledTests.RSAKeyUsage-Client-WantEncipherment-GotE: [policy-difference] static-RSA key-transport (keyEncipherment) cipher suites are not offered - we, like rustls, offer only ECDHE (forward secrecy), so there is no common encipherment suite (TLS 1.3 removes these suites entirely)
DisabledTests.SendClientVersion-RSA: [policy-difference] the peer offers only TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 (static-RSA key transport); we, like rustls, offer only ECDHE (forward secrecy), so there is no common cipher suite and we abort with handshake_failure
DisabledTests.ServerPadding*: [out-of-scope] BoringSSL's client-requested server record padding (-request-server-padding) is a non-standard negotiated mechanism; RFC 8446 5.4 record padding is optional and we, like rustls, do not implement the request extension
DisabledTests.ClientHelloPadding: [policy-difference] the RFC 7685 padding extension (pad a ClientHello into the 256-511 byte range up to 512, a workaround for a specific F5 middlebox bug) is not sent; we, like rustls, do not pad the ClientHello, so its size stays as built
DisabledTests.AllExtensions-Client-Permute*: [out-of-scope] exercises -permute-extensions (randomize ClientHello extension order for fingerprint resistance) bundled with SCT and a kitchen-sink of extensions; we, like rustls, send a deterministic extension order and defer SCT, so the permutation feature is not implemented
DisabledTests.LargeMessage-Reject: [policy-difference] BoringSSL's -max-cert-list caps the peer certificate list at a configurable size; we, like rustls, enforce a fixed handshake-message-size bound instead of that per-connection knob, so we do not reject at the runner's 16384 threshold
DisabledTests.PartialServerHelloWithHelloRetryRequest: [deferred] the server splits the first byte of a HelloRetryRequest into a separate record (P-384 forces the HRR); detecting the excess handshake data requires framing the partially-delivered HRR before the record-layer epoch transition, which currently surfaces as bad_record_mac rather than the excess-handshake-data unexpected_message. A deep record-layer/HRR-interleave fix deferred
DisabledTests.ALPNServer-SelectEmpty-*: [out-of-scope] -select-empty-alpn drives BoringSSL's ALPN-select callback to return an empty protocol (which it then rejects); our server has no configuration that selects an empty ALPN protocol - it only ever selects a non-empty offered one or none - so the scenario is unreachable
DisabledTests.MLKEMKeyShareIncluded*: [policy-difference] BoringSSL sends key_shares for the first classical AND first post-quantum group (to avoid an HRR while bounding ClientHello size); we, like rustls (a single offered_key_share), send one key_share for the most-preferred group
DisabledTests.CustomKeyShares-*: [policy-difference] tests BoringSSL's -key-shares prediction API (send key_shares for a chosen subset - possibly multiple, or a non-most-preferred - of the supported groups); we, like rustls, send a single key_share for the most-preferred group

RFC 4492
DisabledTests.EmptyExtensions-ClientHello-TLS12: [policy-difference] a TLS 1.2 ClientHello with an empty extensions vector offers no supported_groups so ECDHE cannot be negotiated; BoringSSL falls back to a static-RSA suite, which our AEAD+ECDHE-only posture does not implement (nor does rustls). DisabledTests.MaxSendFragment-*: [policy-difference] the RFC 6066 max_fragment_length extension is not implemented; we, like rustls, implement its RFC 8449 replacement record_size_limit instead (RFC 8449 1 deprecates max_fragment_length for its deficiencies), so we never fragment to the client's requested max_fragment_length

_comment_failopenguard: MUST-REJECT negative tests that are disabled only for an ALERT difference (we still reject,
just with a different alert than BoringSSL expects). The classifier force-runs these and
asserts the handshake is still REJECTED - a force-run 'unexpected success' (the shim accepted
what it must reject) is a fail-open regression the disable would otherwise hide, not an alert
difference. Do NOT list permissive policy differences here (ed25519 / P-521 / record-version
acceptance), whose 'unexpected success' is the intended RFC-permitted behavior.
